Comment: Alpha Engine post-close pipeline — the half of the day's close-out that needs only the close: market-hours gate, mutex, deploy-drift check, trading-box start + SSM readiness, executor-checkout refresh, and the live-IB CaptureSnapshot (trades/snapshots/{run_date}.json) with its bounded same-day retry, then the completion marker. Everything that depends on the standalone EOD collection (ne-data-collection-eod, 18:15 ET) — the collection readiness wait, the reconcile precondition probe, EODReconcile and its self-heal loop, the trading-box stop and the weekly-exercise chain — runs in ne-postclose-reconcile-pipeline (infrastructure/step_function_eod_reconcile.json), started when that collection reaches a terminal state. alpha-engine-config-I11269 follow-up (Brian, 2026-09-30: "run all steps in the post close sf that can run immediately after close and just set up the part that relies on the collector as a separate sf"). Triggered by daemon shutdown on the trading EC2 (~16:00 ET); alpha-engine-eod-backstop is the same-day backstop. Leaves the trading box RUNNING on success — see CheckDegradedOutcome.

MarketHoursGate.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I7111 (Brian ruling 2026-08-13, option c) — the "no trading-pipeline start during NYSE market hours" boundary, sited on the PIPELINE rather than on one caller's IAM role. alpha-engine-config#2932 ruled it onto alpha-engine-sf-watch-executor-role, enforced by a Lambda flipping that role's inline policy every 5 minutes between two codified variants. The Lambda never existed in account 711398986525 (measured 2026-08-12: no function, no EventBridge rule), so the boundary was never once in force — and being caller-scoped it could not have covered the in-session operator starts at 09:32 PT on 2026-08-07 or 08:32 PT on 2026-07-27 either. IAM has NO time-of-day condition key; that absence is why the ruled mechanism needed a Lambda to simulate one, and why the simulation could silently not exist for three weeks. A guard state binds every principal: the scheduler, the Overseer's overseer-sf-watch lane, and the operator. Neither existing guard covers this — AcquireMutex keys on the same UTC MINUTE and TradingDayGate on the calendar DAY; neither is a time-of-day boundary. Same zero-infra posture as TradingDayGate: pure calendar math on alpha-engine-predictor-inference, returning BEFORE PredictorPreflight is constructed, so no S3/ArcticDB/model problem can take out the boundary. `now` is $$.Execution.StartTime rather than the Lambda's own clock, so the verdict is a property of the execution: deterministic, replayable, and immune to a slow cold start pushing a refused run past the close. `execution_input` is passed whole because an ASL "override.$": "$.market_hours_override" parameter throws States.Runtime on every run that does not carry one.

MarketHoursGateChoice.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I7111 — the boundary itself. Keys on the gate's verdict, which is enumerated EXHAUSTIVELY: an absent or unrecognised verdict is a contract violation by our own Lambda and fails CLOSED via Default rather than proceeding to trade on an unverifiable answer (the config-I2767 lesson TradingDayGateChoice already carries). PROCEED_OVERRIDE is the ruling's second requirement — the boundary must be refusable deliberately, never bypassable accidentally — and it routes through a notify state so a crossed boundary is announced rather than silent.

Choices.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I7111 / config-I2767, added 2026-08-13. This rule must come FIRST and must be IsPresent-guarded. A Choice rule comparing a path that does not exist raises States.Runtime — it does NOT fall through to Default — so this Choice's own comment claiming an absent verdict 'fails CLOSED via Default' described behaviour ASL does not have. The 2026-08-13 preopen run proved it: verdict absent, States.Runtime at this state, execution dead 48s in with no SNS alert of any kind and no orders placed. Matching here short-circuits before any StringEquals touches the missing path, which is exactly how TradingDayGateChoice has been written since config-I2767.

Market closed. The scheduled trigger of both pipelines lands here every day: preopen at 05:15 PT (pre-open) and postclose at 13:00:0x PT, which is 16:00:0x ET — the session window is half-open [09:30, 16:00) so the close instant itself is already outside it.
In-session start with a complete, authored, unexpired, bounded override. Announced and recorded, never silent.
In-session start with no override — the boundary doing its job.

An override was offered and is not usable. Fails closed whether or not the market is open: a typo'd override is a mis-authorisation, and surfacing it on the quiet run is the only way it is not discovered on the run that matters.

StampMarketHoursVerdictMissing.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I7111. Postclose posture: an unevaluable gate proceeds DEGRADED — settlement and reconciliation must still happen, and the boundary's job at 16:00 ET is already satisfied by the schedule. Routes into the existing degraded pair rather than the preopen refusal, preserving the asymmetry the two pipelines already declare. Stamping $.market_hours_gate_error is required: both SetMarketHoursUnverifiedDegraded and NotifyMarketHoursUnverified read it.

Result.Cause: alpha-engine-config-I7111: the market-hours gate Lambda returned successfully but its payload carried no `verdict` key, so this execution cannot establish that it is starting outside the NYSE session. This is a contract violation by our own producer, not an invoke failure, so the Task's Catch never fires and $.market_hours_gate_error would otherwise be absent. Measured 2026-08-13 (execution 59c0ce46): the `live` alias of alpha-engine-predictor-inference was frozen at a version predating action=check_market_hours, so the invoke fell through to the default predict branch and answered the gate with {statusCode, body}. The full payload received is in $.market_hours_gate.

RecordMarketHoursOverride.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I7111 — the override's audit surface. A crossed boundary is announced on the alert topic AND left in execution history with who authorised it, why, and until when. Catch continues to the pipeline: the authorisation was already validated and recorded, so a notify-side failure must not silently convert an approved recovery into a refusal.

Parameters.Subject: Alpha Engine EOD Pipeline — market-hours boundary OVERRIDDEN (authorised in-session start)
Parameters.Message.$: States.Format('An execution started INSIDE the NYSE regular session under an explicit market-hours override (alpha-engine-config-I7111). Execution: {}. Gate verdict: {}. This is a deliberate, time-boxed authorisation, not a bypass — the same record is in $.market_hours_gate in execution history.', $$.Execution.Id, States.JsonToString($.market_hours_gate.Payload))

Catch.Comment: SNS delivery is the announcement, not the record — the gate verdict and the full override document are in $.market_hours_gate in execution history either way. A publish failure must not change what the boundary decided.

NotifyMarketHoursBlocked.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I7111 — a refusal is loud. sf-pipeline-policy §2.3: a run that did not do its work must not read as a clean success to a status-keyed watcher, so this notifies and then ends in a Fail rather than a Succeed-skip. The message carries the exact override shape so the operator does not have to find it.

Parameters.Subject: Alpha Engine EOD Pipeline — REFUSED (start inside NYSE market hours)
Parameters.Message.$: States.Format('Refused to start a trading pipeline inside the NYSE regular session (alpha-engine-config-I7111). Execution: {}. Gate: {}. To authorise one in-session start, add a market_hours_override object to the execution input carrying reason, authorized_by and expires_at. All three are required and non-blank; expires_at must be an ISO-8601 instant AFTER the execution start and no more than 24h after it, so a line pasted into a runbook stops working instead of standing forever.', $$.Execution.Id, States.JsonToString($.market_hours_gate.Payload))

Catch.Comment: SNS delivery is the announcement, not the record — the gate verdict and the full override document are in $.market_hours_gate in execution history either way. A publish failure must not change what the boundary decided.

MarketHoursBlocked.Cause: alpha-engine-config-I7111: this execution's start time falls inside the NYSE regular session ([09:30, 16:00) ET on a trading day) and carried no market-hours override. Trading pipelines do not start in-session — the preopen chain boots the trading box and starts the order-placing daemon, and the postclose chain stops the box and reconciles the book; either one, mid-session, acts on a stale plan against a live market. The verdict, the ET clock it was judged against, and the override shape are in $.market_hours_gate and in the SNS alert. To authorise one in-session start, re-run with market_hours_override {reason, authorized_by, expires_at}.

NotifyMarketHoursOverrideMalformed.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I7111 — a rejected override is its own terminal, distinct from MarketHoursBlocked, because it calls for a different operator action: fix the override, not wait for the close. Kept separate rather than folded in so a status-keyed watcher can tell the two apart from the Error alone.

Parameters.Subject: Alpha Engine EOD Pipeline — REFUSED (market-hours override is not usable)
Parameters.Message.$: States.Format('A market-hours override was offered and rejected (alpha-engine-config-I7111). Execution: {}. Gate: {}. To authorise one in-session start, add a market_hours_override object to the execution input carrying reason, authorized_by and expires_at. All three are required and non-blank; expires_at must be an ISO-8601 instant AFTER the execution start and no more than 24h after it, so a line pasted into a runbook stops working instead of standing forever.', $$.Execution.Id, States.JsonToString($.market_hours_gate.Payload))

Catch.Comment: SNS delivery is the announcement, not the record — the gate verdict and the full override document are in $.market_hours_gate in execution history either way. A publish failure must not change what the boundary decided.

MarketHoursOverrideMalformed.Cause: alpha-engine-config-I7111: the execution input carried a market_hours_override that is not a usable authorisation — missing or blank reason/authorized_by/expires_at, a non-object, an unparseable expires_at, an expires_at at or before the execution start, or one more than 24h after it. The specific rejection is in $.market_hours_gate.Payload.override.rejection. Deliberately fails closed even when the market is shut: a half-typed override is a mis-authorisation, and it is better found on the run where it did not matter.

NotifyMarketHoursUnverified.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I7111 — the postclose gate fails OPEN, DEGRADED, where the preopen gate fails closed. Three measured reasons, not a preference: (1) sf-pipeline-policy §1.3 makes NAV continuity non-negotiable — every trading day terminates with a postclose completion marker and an eod_pnl.csv row, including days the morning failed; (2) unlike preopen, nothing else in this pipeline touches alpha-engine-predictor-inference, so refusing here would newly break settlement on an outage that is otherwise irrelevant to it; (3) the only automated caller — the daemon at executor/daemon.py, `market_opened and not is_market_hours()` — applies the IDENTICAL predicate before calling StartExecution, and applies it strictly earlier, which is why every observed eod-* execution starts at 16:00:0x ET. The residual is real and stated: while this Lambda is down, an OPERATOR could start postclose in-session and the gate would not stop them — it would say so, loudly, and the run would terminate DEGRADED.

Parameters.Subject: Alpha Engine EOD Pipeline — DEGRADED (market-hours gate could not be evaluated; settlement proceeds)
Parameters.Message.$: States.Format('The market-hours gate Lambda failed after retries (alpha-engine-config-I7111). This execution proceeds DEGRADED rather than refusing. Execution: {}. Error: {}.', $$.Execution.Id, States.JsonToString($.market_hours_gate_error))

Catch.Comment: SNS delivery is the announcement, not the record — the gate verdict and the full override document are in $.market_hours_gate in execution history either way. A publish failure must not change what the boundary decided.

SetMarketHoursUnverifiedDegraded.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I7111 — Option-A parity with SetDataSpotDegradedFlag/SetDegradedFlag (config#6692/config-I2702 shape): threads $.degraded_summary onto the market-hours fail-open path WITHOUT changing its continuation, so CheckDegradedOutcome routes this execution's terminal to WriteCompletionMarkerDegraded/DegradedRun. A settlement run that could not verify its own start boundary is not a clean success. Last-write-wins if a later stage also degrades.

CheckMutexRole.Comment: L274 SF MutualExclusionGuard — gate at SF entry point. Allowlist all unattended cadence-roles (currently: daily / weekly / eod / shell-run / exercise) acquire the DynamoDB mutex; absent/operator/recovery/smoke/backfill/operator-replay roles bypass entirely (operator-initiated runs are deliberately concurrent with cadence runs). Daemon-triggered EOD launches set pipeline_role='eod' (executor/daemon.py::_trigger_eod_pipeline); operator-launched replays MUST set their own pipeline_role per the taxonomy in pipeline-reporting-revamp-260524.md §6. Closes the architectural hole the L286a/b producer-side universe_writer_lock covers for manual daily_append invocations — that lock guards the data writer; this Choice guards the SF entry point. Together they cover both halves of single-writer-per-cadence-cell.

AcquireMutex.Comment: L274 — DynamoDB conditional PUT. mutex_key = '{state-machine-name}#{pipeline_role}#{YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM}' (UTC minute bucket parsed from $$.Execution.StartTime). Two duplicate cron-fired executions started in the same minute produce identical keys; the second loses with ConditionalCheckFailedException → MutexConflict Fail. No TTL / no release: the date+minute in the key is itself the staleness window. Item accumulation ~<1000/yr; PAY_PER_REQUEST cost negligible.

Catch.Comment: Mutex held by another concurrent execution in the same minute bucket — the duplicate-trigger case we are explicitly protecting against. Fail loud (EOD has its own ForceStopInstance cost-guard on the failure path, so a MutexConflict still releases the trading instance).

Fail-open: DynamoDB outage / IAM drift / transient SDK error must NOT block the snapshot capture. The mutex is best-effort architectural insurance; per feedback_no_silent_fails 'secondary observability' carve-out, the primary deliverable (the close-time IB snapshot) survives a mutex-side failure. The error is captured in $.mutex_error for forensic review. alpha-engine-config#6722: routes through SetMutexAcquireDegradedFlag so CheckDegradedOutcome's terminal reflects it.

SetMutexAcquireDegradedFlag.Comment: alpha-engine-config#6722 (Option-A parity, config#6692/config-I2702 shape): threads $.degraded_summary onto the mutex-acquire infra-error fail-open path (DynamoDB outage / IAM drift / transient SDK error — NOT the ConditionalCheckFailedException conflict case, which the separate MutexConflict Fail already handles) WITHOUT changing its fail-open continuation. Last-write-wins if a later stage also degrades. Does not clobber $.mutex_error (set by AcquireMutex's own Catch ResultPath).

MutexConflict.Cause: L274: another EOD execution with the same pipeline_role + start-minute already holds the mutex. Cost-guard note: the EOD SF's HandleFailure → ForceStopInstance chain is unreachable from a Fail state, but a duplicate EOD execution by definition means another EOD execution IS running the cost-guard path; the trading instance still gets stopped.

StartTradingInstance.Comment: Re-runnability guard (2026-06-30 incident). Ensure the long-lived trading instance is running + SSM-registered BEFORE any ssm:sendCommand. The normal daemon-shutdown-triggered run enters with the box already up, but the failure-path ForceStopInstance (here and in ne-postclose-reconcile-pipeline) and the reconcile pipeline's own StopTradingInstance all STOP it — so any operator or eod-backstop rerun lands on a stopped instance and the first sendCommand would die with Ssm.InvalidInstanceIdException. ec2:startInstances is a no-op if already running, so this is safe on the normal path and makes the pipeline idempotently re-runnable. Mirrors the daily/preopen StartExecutorEC2 -> SSM-readiness poll (config#1430).

WaitForInstanceReady.Comment: Initial settle before polling for SSM-agent registration. EC2 stopped→running takes ~15-25s; polling describeInstanceInformation any earlier just burns API calls.

InitSSMPollCounter.Comment: Initialize attempts counter for the SSM-readiness poll loop.

DescribeInstanceInfo.Comment: Poll SSM-agent registration on the trading instance until PingStatus=Online, so the first EOD ssm:sendCommand never fires against a stopped / not-yet-registered box (the Ssm.InvalidInstanceIdException failure mode). Mirrors the daily SF DescribeInstanceInfo (config#1430).

SSMReadyChoice.Comment: PingStatus=Online -> CheckSkipRefreshExecutorDeploy (the first per-task rerun gate; the executor-checkout refresh is hoisted to the top of the pipeline per config#1549 so CaptureSnapshot executes latest origin/main by construction). Otherwise wait + retry up to 12 attempts (~3 min total budget). Hard-fail to HandleFailure when the budget is exhausted (per feedback_no_silent_fails — the agent not registering after 3 min is a real boot problem, not just timing; HandleFailure notifies + ForceStopInstance releases the box). This NEVER silently skips CaptureSnapshot — an unreachable box fails the execution loud.

SetSSMReadyExhaustedError.Comment: Normalize SSM-ready exhaustion into $.error so HandleFailure's States.JsonToString($.error) has an object to serialize — the Choice path from SSMReadyChoice does not carry a caught error (the SSM DescribeInstanceInfo calls succeeded; the agent simply never went Online). Without this, HandleFailure itself crashes with States.Runtime on the missing $.error JsonPath, masking the real 'trading instance unreachable' cause behind a broken error-reporting state.

Parameters.error: SSM agent did not come Online within 12 attempts (~3 min) — the trading instance is unreachable. The EOD pipeline cannot proceed without an SSM connection to the box (every work step is SSM:sendCommand).

CaptureSnapshot.Comment: Capture live IB state once at the close and persist it to s3://alpha-engine-research/trades/snapshots/{run_date}.json. EODReconcile (now in ne-postclose-reconcile-pipeline) reads that snapshot instead of querying live IB, so the row keyed by run_date=X sources from observations made at time X. alpha-engine-config-I11269 follow-up (Brian, 2026-09-30: "run all steps in the post close sf that can run immediately after close and just set up the part that relies on the collector as a separate sf"): this state used to run ~3.5 h after the close, behind the bounded wait on ne-data-collection-eod (18:15 ET = dates.SETTLED_AFTER_ET); it needs nothing from the collector, so it now runs minutes after the daemon-shutdown trigger — the snapshot records the book AT the close, which is what it was always meant to record.

Parameters.commands.$: States.Array('set -o pipefail', 'cd /home/ec2-user/alpha-engine', 'export AWS_REGION=us-east-1 AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1', 'export ALPHA_ENGINE_DEPLOYED=1', 'export FLOW_DOCTOR_ENABLED=1', 'source .venv/bin/activate', States.Format('python -m krepis.ssm_log_capture run --correlation-id {} --slug snapshot --log /var/log/snapshot.log -- python executor/snapshot_capturer.py --date {}', $$.Execution.Name, $.run_date))

Catch.Comment: config#5569: routes into the bounded same-day retry (CheckCaptureSnapshotRetryBudget) instead of straight to HandleFailure. The retry is bounded at 1 and the EVENTUAL failure after it is exhausted still reaches HandleFailure hard — EODReconcile (in ne-postclose-reconcile-pipeline) depends on this snapshot and there is deliberately NO silent fallback to live IB.
config#5569: same bounded same-day retry as CaptureSnapshot's own Catch — a persistent SSM poll failure on this stage is treated as a capture failure, not routed straight to hard-fail.

CheckSnapshotStatus.Comment: Success -> CheckDegradedOutcome (this pipeline's deliverable, the S3 snapshot, now exists). Default routes to SnapshotStatusError -> the bounded same-day retry so any unexpected SSM status is surfaced, not silently swallowed.

SnapshotStatusError.Comment: Choice Default path — synthesize $.error from poll result. config#5569: routes into the bounded same-day retry, not straight to HandleFailure.

CheckCaptureSnapshotRetryBudget.Comment: config#5569 deliverable #1: CaptureSnapshot has an irreversible per-day deadline the generic re-runnable EOD stages do not (alpha-engine-config-I5325 lost 2026-07-27 permanently when this stage failed with no same-day retry). Bounded at exactly 1 retry, mirroring CheckDataSpotRetryBudget's one-retry-then-terminal policy — the FIRST failure pages immediately (PageCaptureSnapshotFailureImmediate) and retries once; a SECOND consecutive failure is the exhausted/irreversible-deadline path. $.capture_snapshot_retry is always initialized by InitCaptureSnapshotRetryCounter before this state is reachable.

PageCaptureSnapshotFailureImmediate.Comment: config#5569 deliverable #2 (immediate half): page SAME-DAY on the FIRST CaptureSnapshot failure, before the bounded retry below even runs — so an operator has the whole retry window to react instead of learning about it only if the retry also fails. Own Catch (mirrors PublishDataSpotFailureImmediate's SNS-with-own-Catch shape) so an SNS-side failure cannot block the retry path.

Parameters.Subject: Alpha Engine EOD CaptureSnapshot failed — same-day retry in flight
Parameters.Message.$: States.Format('CaptureSnapshot failed for run_date={}. This stage has NO next-day recovery path: eod_reconcile requires the S3 snapshot to exist and it cannot be reconstructed after midnight (alpha-engine-config-I5325 lost 2026-07-27 this way). One bounded same-day retry is launching now — if it ALSO fails this pages again as an IRREVERSIBLE-DEADLINE failure requiring action before midnight. Detail: {}', $.run_date, States.JsonToString($.error))

IncrementCaptureSnapshotRetry.Comment: config#5569: consume the single same-day retry — no force_on_demand analog (CaptureSnapshot runs on the already-running trading box via SSM, not a spot dispatcher).

CaptureSnapshotRetryExhausted.Comment: config#5569: the single same-day retry has now also failed — this IS the irreversible-deadline moment: trades/snapshots/{run_date}.json will not exist and eod_reconcile can never run for run_date after midnight (alpha-engine-config-I5325 precedent, lost 2026-07-27). Normalize a distinct error payload ahead of the terminal page + HandleFailure.

PageCaptureSnapshotIrreversibleFailure.Comment: config#5569 deliverable #2 (terminal half): a DISTINCT same-day page from the ordinary EOD-stage HandleFailure notify — marked IRREVERSIBLE-DEADLINE because the required operator response differs (act before midnight UTC or the day's correction path is permanently gone; there is no tomorrow for this one). Own Catch (mirrors PublishDataSpotFailureImmediate's SNS-with-own-Catch shape) so an SNS-side failure cannot block the hard-fail path into HandleFailure. HandleFailure remains the terminal sink — this stage still hard-fails with NO silent fallback to live IB, that constraint is deliberate (Phase 2 cutover) and unchanged by this retry.

Parameters.Subject: Alpha Engine EOD CaptureSnapshot IRREVERSIBLE FAILURE — act before midnight
Parameters.Message.$: States.Format('CaptureSnapshot failed twice for run_date={} (same-day retry budget exhausted). trades/snapshots/{}.json will NOT exist and eod_reconcile CANNOT run for this date after midnight UTC — the correction path is permanently gone (alpha-engine-config-I5325, lost 2026-07-27 the same way). This needs a same-day operator response now, not next-day reconcile_audit triage. Detail: {}', $.run_date, $.run_date, States.JsonToString($.error))

CheckSkipRefreshExecutorDeploy.Comment: Per-task rerun gate (L4607) for the top-of-pipeline executor-deploy refresh (config#1549). Input {"skip_refresh_executor_deploy": true} (operator-replay only) routes past RefreshExecutorDeploy straight to CheckSkipCaptureSnapshot; missing flag = run as normal. This is the FIRST gate the SSM-ready path enters, so CaptureSnapshot executes latest origin/main by construction. alpha-engine-config-I11269 follow-up (Brian, 2026-09-30: "run all steps in the post close sf that can run immediately after close and just set up the part that relies on the collector as a separate sf"): the collector-dependent stages it used to precede (the collection readiness wait, the precondition probe, EODReconcile and its heal loop) moved to ne-postclose-reconcile-pipeline, which carries its own copy of this gate and refresh because it may boot the box itself.

RefreshExecutorDeploy.Comment:
Hoisted deploy-drift chokepoint (config#1549), NARROWED to a conditional refresh (alpha-engine-config-I2722, 2026-07-16): fetches origin and compares local HEAD to origin/main FIRST; the expensive boot-pull.sh (multi-repo pull + pip install + systemd-unit sync + trades.db restore, up to the full 600s budget) only runs when the checkout has actually drifted. A hard-fail-on-any-invocation reading would false-fail every day an intraday executor merge lands (the exact scenario this chokepoint exists to catch), since boot-pull.sh's own boot-pull.service only fires on instance boot. Original rationale retained below for the drifted path, which is UNCHANGED byte-for-byte.

Refreshes the trading instance's crucible-executor checkout to origin/main via the canonical boot-pull.sh ONCE at the top of the EOD pipeline, before any work step runs. The trading instance boot-pulls once each morning (boot-pull.service, ~6:10 AM PT), but executor PRs that merge during the trading day leave the checkout stale by EOD (2026-06-30 incident: 3 executor PRs merged 08:07–08:54 PT after the morning boot-pull). nousergon-data#574 patched only the EODReconcile step (the one work step carrying a drift guard); the earlier PostMarketData / PostMarketArcticAppend / CaptureSnapshot steps had no guard and would run stale intraday code silently. Refreshing here makes the whole run execute latest main by construction. FAIL-LOUD: boot-pull runs WITHOUT a `|| echo` swallow, so a failed refresh (auth/network/dep-install) surfaces as a non-zero SSM status → HandleFailure → ForceStopInstance BEFORE any stale-code work step runs (stronger than #574, whose swallow relied on the downstream reconcile guard). boot-pull runs as ec2-user (matching boot-pull.service User=ec2-user + the ec2-user-owned checkout / ~/.netrc); a root git fetch/reset would trip git's dubious-ownership guard (CVE-2022-24765). Re-freezes /home/ec2-user/.frozen_executor_sha to the just-refreshed HEAD (2026-07-09 incident, config#2042): config#1955's morning CodeFreshnessGate pin is what eod_reconcile.py's ExecutorPreflight.check_deploy_drift actually validates against — this step's premise ('the guard remains authoritative because the box now matches latest main') silently stopped holding the moment #1955 shipped a FIXED T0 pin file instead of a live-origin/main comparison. Two same-day executor PRs (#345, #346) merged between the morning freeze and this step, so the box moved past the stale morning pin and EODReconcile hard-failed 36min later with zero eod_report.json for the day. Re-freezing here — mirroring CodeFreshnessGate's own rev-parse-HEAD-to-pin-file line exactly — keeps the pin in lockstep with what this step just deployed, restoring the invariant the chokepoint comment already assumed. The fast (not-drifted) path also re-freezes the pin unconditionally (cheap, idempotent) rather than assuming it's already correct, so the lockstep invariant holds regardless of which branch ran.

commands: echo "checkout drifted (local=$LOCAL_SHA remote=$REMOTE_SHA) -- running full refresh"

Catch.Comment: Fail-loud: a failed executor-deploy refresh must halt EOD before any work step runs stale code. Don't paper over it — the whole point of the hoist is that non-guarded steps never run stale.

CheckRefreshExecutorDeployStatus.Comment: Default routes to HandleFailure so any unexpected SSM status (Failed, Cancelled, TimedOut, ...) is surfaced, not silently swallowed — a stale checkout must never reach the work steps.

RefreshExecutorDeployStatusError.Comment: Choice Default path — synthesize $.error from poll result so HandleFailure's JsonToString($.error) has something to stringify.

CheckSkipCaptureSnapshot.Comment: Per-task rerun gate (L4607). Input {"skip_capture_snapshot": true} (operator-replay only) routes past CaptureSnapshot straight to the terminal decision; missing flag = run as normal. Skip only when the snapshot trades/snapshots/{run_date}.json already exists from a prior run. alpha-engine-config-I11269 follow-up (Brian, 2026-09-30: "run all steps in the post close sf that can run immediately after close and just set up the part that relies on the collector as a separate sf"): this pipeline's work ends at CaptureSnapshot; reconciliation is ne-postclose-reconcile-pipeline's.

InitCaptureSnapshotRetryCounter.Comment: config#5569: retry budget for the same-day bounded CaptureSnapshot retry — mirrors InitDataSpotRetryCounter. CaptureSnapshot is the EOD pipeline's only stage with an irreversible per-day deadline (trades/snapshots/{run_date}.json must exist before midnight or eod_reconcile's correction path is permanently gone — alpha-engine-config-I5325 lost 2026-07-27 this way), so unlike the generic re-runnable stages this counter exists specifically to bound ONE same-day retry before the terminal irreversible-deadline page.

CheckDegradedOutcome.Comment: config-I2702 deliverable #4: the ONE place that decides which terminal this execution reaches. $.degraded_summary is set by any Set*DegradedFlag state this execution passed (market-hours gate unverified, mutex fail-open, deploy-drift degrade/observe). alpha-engine-config-I11269 follow-up (Brian, 2026-09-30: "run all steps in the post close sf that can run immediately after close and just set up the part that relies on the collector as a separate sf"): this pipeline no longer stops the trading box on its success path. Measured before the split, the box was up from the ~16:00 ET close until this pipeline's StopTradingInstance at ~19:30-21:47 ET, and three co-tenant units on the box are scheduled inside that window and rely on it: crucible-executor alpha-engine-trader-reconcile.timer (16:45 America/New_York, moved there by alpha-engine-config-I11545 precisely to clear the measured v1 stop), alpha-engine-eod-reconcile-standalone.timer (21:05 UTC) and alpha-engine-reference-rate-publish.timer (21:15 UTC). Stopping the box minutes after the close would kill all three every day. The box's uptime envelope is therefore unchanged by the split: ne-postclose-reconcile-pipeline stops it after EODReconcile, exactly where this pipeline used to, and the 22:00 PT alpha-engine-stop-trading schedule remains the cost-guard backstop if the reconcile pipeline never runs. The failure path is unchanged: HandleFailure -> ForceStopInstance still releases the box on any hard failure here.

Choices.Comment: config-I2767 (2026-07-16 incident): $.degraded_summary is only assigned on a degraded path — on a fully-green day the path is ABSENT and an unguarded dereference threw States.Runtime, failing the execution at its very last state. Absent flag = never degraded = NormalSucceeded via Default, which is the semantically exact reading, so no separate malformed route is needed here.

WriteCompletionMarkerNormal.Comment: config#2857: SF-envelope completion marker — an end-of-SF terminal artifact, independent of downstream pipeline deliverables, that proves THIS Step Functions execution reached its real success terminal (config#1724 independent-signal doctrine). Written on the normal outcome, immediately before the distinct NormalSucceeded terminal (config-I2702 deliverable #4 keeps Normal/Degraded as separate named states for the console/notification signal — this marker preserves that split rather than converging them, since both routes must still each reach their own named Succeed). Registered in ARTIFACT_REGISTRY.yaml as sf_completion_ne_postclose_trading_pipeline (cadence eod_sf). No swallow-all Catch here (unlike the SNS notifiers' config#1819 pattern): Retry covers transient S3 faults, but a marker that genuinely cannot be written means this execution's own completion is unverifiable — exactly the ambiguity this feature exists to surface, not mask.

Retry.Comment: Transient S3 fault coverage — mirrors the SendCommand SDK-transient Retry convention used elsewhere in this SF.

NormalSucceeded.Comment: The ordinary, fully-green terminal — CaptureSnapshot ran (or was validly skipped via an operator-replay skip_capture_snapshot flag), nothing degraded. The trading box is left RUNNING for ne-postclose-reconcile-pipeline (see CheckDegradedOutcome).

WriteCompletionMarkerDegraded.Comment: config#2857: SF-envelope completion marker — an end-of-SF terminal artifact, independent of downstream pipeline deliverables, that proves THIS Step Functions execution reached its real success terminal (config#1724 independent-signal doctrine). Written on the degraded outcome, immediately before the DegradedRun Fail terminal (config-I2702 deliverable #4 + Brian's 2026-07-28 Option-A ruling, alpha-engine-config#2699: the marker still fires so the completion artifact exists, but DegradedRun is Type: Fail so status-keyed watchers engage). Registered in ARTIFACT_REGISTRY.yaml as sf_completion_ne_postclose_trading_pipeline (cadence eod_sf). No swallow-all Catch here (unlike the SNS notifiers' config#1819 pattern): Retry covers transient S3 faults, but a marker that genuinely cannot be written means this execution's own completion is unverifiable — exactly the ambiguity this feature exists to surface, not mask. ResultPath is LOAD-BEARING, not hygiene (alpha-engine-config-I6891): a Task with no ResultPath defaults to $, so the putObject result REPLACES the whole state input and the DegradedRun terminal's CausePath dereference of $.degraded_summary.reason cannot resolve. The execution then fails with States.Runtime instead of DegradedRun — and Error: DegradedRun is a consumer contract: sf-telegram-notifier's _is_degraded_run() keys its DEGRADED rendering off exactly that string, so every honestly-degraded run rendered as an ordinary crash-red FAILED with a truncated cause. Shipped in both weekday definitions since config#6692/#6722; the weekly one inherited it by mirroring them and it is fixed in all three here.

Retry.Comment: Transient S3 fault coverage — mirrors the SendCommand SDK-transient Retry convention used elsewhere in this SF.

DegradedRun.CausePath: States.Format('EOD pipeline DEGRADED — reason: {}. Full degraded_summary: {}. Per the 2026-07-28 Option-A ruling (alpha-engine-config#2699): a degraded run must FAIL so status-keyed watchers (sf-watch, EventBridge, sf-telegram-notifier) engage with zero new plumbing. The trading box is left running for ne-postclose-reconcile-pipeline, which stops it after EODReconcile.', $.degraded_summary.reason, States.JsonToString($.degraded_summary))
DegradedRun.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I6856: the Cause is DERIVED from $.degraded_summary, never an enumeration of the paths that can reach here. It WAS an enumeration, and it drifted — 4 states set $.degraded_summary in this definition before the alpha-engine-config-I11269-follow-up split (SetDataSpotDegradedFlag, SetDegradedFlag, SetMutexAcquireDegradedFlag, SetWeeklyExerciseDegradedFlag) and the hardcoded string named one. On 2026-08-11 the preopen terminal asserted 'run_daemon_restart_failed and/or daily_data_spot_fail_open' when neither fired; the real reason, daily_scanner_fail_open, appeared nowhere, and the message sent the operator hunting for a PublishDataSpotFailureImmediate event that could not exist on that path. An enumeration that drifts is worse than boilerplate because it reads as specific (sf-pipeline-policy.md §2.3 corollary). $.degraded_summary.reason is dereferenced UNGUARDED on purpose: CheckDegradedOutcome only routes here when degraded is true, every Set*DegradedFlag state sets reason, and tests/test_degraded_terminal_derives_its_cause.py fails the build if a new one does not — a defensive fallback here would let that guarantee lapse silently. JsonToString takes the WHOLE summary rather than $.degraded_summary.stage_error, which not every path sets.

HandleFailure.Comment: Failure alert via SNS — instance still stops to avoid cost. ARN is hardcoded (not $.sns_topic_arn) so a malformed input field can never block the cost-guard. Catch routes to ForceStopInstance so any SNS-side failure (throttling, IAM drift, transient outage) still stops the instance.

Parameters.Subject: Alpha Engine EOD Pipeline — FAILED
Parameters.Message.$: States.Format('EOD pipeline failed. Error: {}. View the failing state + per-state detail at https://dashboard.nousergon.ai/pipeline-status', States.JsonToString($.error))

Catch.Comment: Defense-in-depth: SNS publish failure must NOT block ForceStopInstance. The cost-guard fires regardless of alert delivery (avoids the 2026-05-14 incident where a malformed sns_topic_arn left the trading instance running).

ForceStopInstance.Comment: Always stop trading instance even on failure — avoid cost overrun

FailExecution.Cause: EOD pipeline failed — trading instance stopped, check logs.

DeployDriftCheck.Comment: alpha-engine-config-I8102. Asks the predictor probe whether the EOD orchestration about to run is the one nousergon-data@main describes, by canonical-JSON comparison of the DEPLOYED definition body against the copy deploy-infrastructure.sh published to S3 (I7799/I7927 semantics, the same predicate the preopen pipeline has enforced since 2026-08-21). sf_name is explicit: without it the probe answers about the PREOPEN state machine and this gate would read a verdict about a pipeline that is not itself (crucible-predictor-PR545 made the key load-bearing and made an undeclared name RAISE rather than silently fall through to stamp semantics). Sited here — after the mutex, before StartTradingInstance — so the question is asked before this pipeline spends anything, per sf-pipeline-policy §2.2. OBSERVE MODE (sf-pipeline-policy §7a, clause SFP-7a-new-guard-observes-first). PROMOTION CRITERION: after 10 consecutive postclose executions in which this gate reached StartTradingInstance without routing here, OR on 2026-09-08, whichever comes first, the three would-halt branches of DeployDriftGate and DeployDriftCheck's Catch flip their Next to HandleFailure and these two observe-only Pass states are deleted. That is the whole promotion diff. Tracked with a Re-exam date on the issue named in the PR body; a guard parked in observe mode indefinitely is the failure §7a exists to prevent, not its goal.

Catch.Comment: The probe itself could not answer — invoke failure, timeout, or the UnknownAction/ValueError crucible-predictor-PR545 raises for an undeclared sf_name. That is an UNMEASURED verdict, never a pass (§2.3a rule 2). At promotion this Next becomes HandleFailure, which is what the preopen definition already does; during the observe window it pages and proceeds.

DeployDriftGate.Comment:
alpha-engine-config-I8102 — the postclose twin of the preopen DeployDriftGate, with the SAME branch families and a DIFFERENT argument for them, because the two pipelines fail differently.

Why sf_drift is a HALT family here, not a degrade: the EOD pipeline writes the day's book — the position snapshot, EODReconcile, the eod_pnl row, the NAV the next morning's planner and every report read. If the deployed orchestration differs from what main describes, the SEQUENCE that produces those numbers is unknown, so a run that completes is asserting a guarantee nobody established (§2.3a rule 3, principles §2.7). A silently wrong EOD is worse than a halted one, and unlike preopen there is no market-open deadline: a lost postclose run costs a mechanical rerun (weekday_sf_rerun.py, §2.5), not an unmanaged real-money session. That asymmetry is the whole reason I7799 moved the preopen gate OFF the stamp, and it does not transfer.

Why it does not halt YET: §7a — a check newly added to a scheduled pipeline path whose verdict can fail a run observes before it enforces. This gate's blast radius on THIS path has never been observed, and §1.3 makes that expensive to get wrong: every trading day must terminate with a postclose completion marker and an eod_pnl row, INCLUDING days when nothing traded — position marks and NAV are facts about the book, not about the pipeline. A false halt here therefore does not merely lose a run, it puts a hole in NAV continuity. §7a.2's own precedent is an EOD gap of exactly this shape: a correct guard whose unobserved blast radius took the price-append and reconcile path down with it. OBSERVE MODE (sf-pipeline-policy §7a, clause SFP-7a-new-guard-observes-first). PROMOTION CRITERION: after 10 consecutive postclose executions in which this gate reached StartTradingInstance without routing here, OR on 2026-09-08, whichever comes first, the three would-halt branches of DeployDriftGate and DeployDriftCheck's Catch flip their Next to HandleFailure and these two observe-only Pass states are deleted. That is the whole promotion diff. Tracked with a Re-exam date on the issue named in the PR body; a guard parked in observe mode indefinitely is the failure §7a exists to prevent, not its goal.

Choices.Comment: sf_drift=true — the deployed postclose definition differs from the one the last deploy published. Orchestration semantics for the run that writes the day's NAV are unknown. HALT family (§3); routed to the observe path until promotion.

sf_drift absent — the probe could not measure definition freshness. Fail CLOSED on unknown, the convention config-I2767 set and I7799 preserved: an unmeasured field is never a pass. HALT family; observe path until promotion.
cf_drift absent — the gate cannot classify a drift signal as halt-vs-degrade without it, so it may not silently pick either. HALT family; observe path until promotion.

cf_drift=true with the definition intact is CloudFormation stack state/template drift — orchestration METADATA, not the sequence that writes the book. §3 degrades and pages. This branch is non-halting by design and stays non-halting after promotion (config-I6615, the 2026-08-05/07 case).

deploy_stamp_stale=true — nousergon-data has merged something it has not deployed, reaching a Lambda, collector or script this pipeline INVOKES but does not embed. Real, and not a reason to skip the day's reconcile: degrades and pages (I7799). Evaluated after cf_drift so a cf_drift degrade is not relabelled, and before Default. Deliberately not IsPresent-guarded toward failure: an absent key means a predictor Lambda older than I7799, whose sf_drift IS the stamp verdict and is enforced one branch up, more strictly.

SetDeployDriftObserveWouldHaltFlag.Comment: OBSERVE-MODE ONLY, deleted at promotion. Records that DeployDriftGate took a HALT-family branch and did not halt. Writes $.degraded_summary in the Option-A shape (config#6692) the EOD's other degrade flags use, so CheckDegradedOutcome routes this execution's terminal to WriteCompletionMarkerDegraded/DegradedRun rather than a plain SUCCEEDED marker — the observe verdict is a real ERROR on a real surface, distinguishable from the enforcing one only by what it does to the run (§7a obligation 3), never a suppression. OBSERVE MODE (sf-pipeline-policy §7a, clause SFP-7a-new-guard-observes-first). PROMOTION CRITERION: after 10 consecutive postclose executions in which this gate reached StartTradingInstance without routing here, OR on 2026-09-08, whichever comes first, the three would-halt branches of DeployDriftGate and DeployDriftCheck's Catch flip their Next to HandleFailure and these two observe-only Pass states are deleted. That is the whole promotion diff. Tracked with a Re-exam date on the issue named in the PR body; a guard parked in observe mode indefinitely is the failure §7a exists to prevent, not its goal.

SetDeployDriftProbeUnreadableFlag.Comment: OBSERVE-MODE ONLY, deleted at promotion. DeployDriftCheck's Catch target: the probe raised or timed out, so there is no $.drift_result.Payload to read and the would-halt Pass above would itself raise States.Runtime on it. Carries $.drift_error instead. Same reason family, distinct value, so the page says WHICH unmeasured shape occurred. OBSERVE MODE (sf-pipeline-policy §7a, clause SFP-7a-new-guard-observes-first). PROMOTION CRITERION: after 10 consecutive postclose executions in which this gate reached StartTradingInstance without routing here, OR on 2026-09-08, whichever comes first, the three would-halt branches of DeployDriftGate and DeployDriftCheck's Catch flip their Next to HandleFailure and these two observe-only Pass states are deleted. That is the whole promotion diff. Tracked with a Re-exam date on the issue named in the PR body; a guard parked in observe mode indefinitely is the failure §7a exists to prevent, not its goal.

SetDeployDriftDegradedFlag.Comment: The permanently NON-HALTING branch of DeployDriftGate: the deployed postclose definition matches what the deploy published, and a condition that is real but not book-correctness-critical is true — cf_drift (CloudFormation stack state) and/or deploy_stamp_stale (merged-but-undeployed code this pipeline invokes). Both degrade per §3. WHICH one fired is carried in stage_error rather than in this state's static reason, because a Choice cannot format a message per branch. Parity with SetMutexAcquireDegradedFlag/SetDataSpotDegradedFlag (config#6692 Option-A); last write wins if a later stage also degrades. Survives promotion unchanged.

PublishDeployDriftDegraded.Comment: One page for all three non-Default routes. It interpolates ONLY $.degraded_summary.reason and the summary itself — both written by whichever Pass state routed here, so no path can leave a States.Format argument unresolvable. That matters more than naming the probe's fields inline: a States.Runtime here would be swallowed by this state's own Catch and the page would be lost precisely on the paths that most need it (the preopen twin's Comment records the same hazard). TopicArn is the literal alerts ARN, not $.sns_topic_arn, matching every other publish in this definition — a malformed input field must not be able to silence the alert. Its Catch leads onward to StartTradingInstance so an SNS outage can never convert a degrade into a halt.

Parameters.Subject: Alpha Engine EOD Pipeline — DEGRADED (deploy drift; EOD proceeds)
Parameters.Message.$: States.Format('DeployDriftGate degraded this EOD run without halting it. reason={} — eod_deploy_drift_observe_would_halt means the gate took a HALT-family branch and did NOT halt because it is still in sf-pipeline-policy 7a observe mode: READ THIS ONE, it is what the enforcing gate would have stopped. eod_deploy_drift_observe_probe_unreadable means the probe could not answer at all. deploy_drift_nonhalting is the permanent degrade family (cf_drift and/or deploy_stamp_stale) and proceeds by design. This execution will complete DEGRADED, not SUCCEEDED. Full summary: {}', $.degraded_summary.reason, States.JsonToString($.degraded_summary))

NormalizeEODFailureContext.Comment: alpha-engine-config#5950. HandleFailure formats States.JsonToString($.error), and three inbound edges never set it: MarketHoursGateChoice's Default, and PageCaptureSnapshotIrreversibleFailure's Next (ResultPath $.capture_snapshot_irreversible_notify) and Catch (no ResultPath). On those paths the EOD pipeline's own failure REPORTER raised States.Runtime, which no Catch can see, so the run died with the reporting error in place of the real one. The weekly SF closed this exact shape with NormalizeFailureContext (alpha-engine-config#2281); this mirrors that pattern rather than inventing a second one, per the shared-code rule. Edges that DO set $.error are left pointing straight at HandleFailure -- the JsonMerge puts the real error above this floor anyway, but not re-routing them keeps the diff to the broken paths.

Parameters.merged.$: States.JsonMerge(States.StringToJson('{"error":{"phase":"Unknown","source":"NormalizeEODFailureContext","detail":"no error was set by the upstream Catch or Choice edge"}}'),$,false)
